anomalies.observed: Both 25 MHz crystals are routed to GPIO pins instead of the MCUs' HSE pins. HSE3 connects NET0131/NET0020 to FCC2 PE6/PE7 (pins 5/37), while FCC2 PH0/PH1 (pins 12/13) are connected to C61/C80. HSE1 connects NET0015/NET0173 to NAVC2 PC3/PC4 (pins 11/24), while NAVC2 PH0/PH1 (pins 5/6) are connected to C59/C89.
anomalies.expected: Each crystal should connect to its MCU's HSE oscillator pins, PH0 and PH1, with appropriate load capacitors. The crystals should not be connected to GPIO pins.

evidence.quote: HSE3: NET0131 ... NET0020; FCC2: PE6 pin 5 NET0131, PE7 pin 37 NET0020; PH0 pin 12 and PH1 pin 13 connect to C61/C80. (FCC sheet, page 2)
HSE1: NET0015 ... NET0173; NAVC2: PC3 pin 11 NET0015, PC4 pin 24 NET0173; PH0 pin 5 and PH1 pin 6 connect to C59/C89. (NAVC sheet, page 3)

anomalies.impact: The external 25 MHz clock sources cannot drive either MCU's HSE oscillator. The GPIO pins instead receive the crystal networks, and the actual HSE pins are not connected to the crystals; clock startup or operation using the intended external clock will fail.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: both MCU crystal networks are routed to GPIO pins rather than the HSE oscillator pins. This prevents the specified external 25 MHz clocks from operating as intended.
